author: Times Radio
description:
“The original agreement said it would last as long as NATO lasts. This agreement Trump says… would last until forever.”

Trump’s new Greenland agreement differs from the original 1951 agreement by extending US presence in Greenland beyond the life of NATO, essentially “stitching up” their presence there forever, says director of the Marie Colvin Centre for International Reporting Sarah Baxter.

Sarah Baxter was speaking to Jane Mulkerrins on Times Radio. Listen live every Saturday 1pm-4pm.

description:
“It’s almost become like an identity or a badge of honour.”

As more buzzwords around mental health are being thrown around, those with a mental health condition should not let it become their identity says The Times columnist and Psychologist Professor Tanya Byron. 

Professor Tanya Bryon was talking to Jane Mulkerrins on Times Radio. Listen every Saturday 1pm-4pm.

description:
“What is the financial benefit of doing this for the government in circumstances where the gains are, relatively speaking, compared to what the exchequer needs to raise, quite modest?”

The suggested mansion tax changes is about “uniting the progressive vote”, but it’s unlikely it would go far in plugging the treasury gap, says deputy political editor for The Sunday Times Lara Spirit.

Lara Spirit was speaking to Ed Vaizey on Times Radio. Listen Live every Friday 10am-1pm.

author: Times Radio
description:
“He has not succeeded in his initial mission, which was to make Greenland part of the USA.”

President Donald Trump saw there was “too much opposition” to his initial plans to make Greenland part of the US, but has now spun the narrative that he is happy with the new deal, says Washington editor for The Times and Sunday Times Katy Balls.

Katy Balls was speaking to Ed Vaizey on Times Radio. Listen Live every Friday 10am-1pm.
